clue.text: Relish boat getting in winning position

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat
a player who is ahead in a game is said to be up

explanation.surface: A yacht nosing into the lead in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomato sauce of this kind is a condiment, which is what relish means here.

clue.text: Overcome with laughter and delight? Not he!

parts.note: 'you kill me' means you make me helpless with laughter, so to kill is to overcome with laughter
joy means delight

explanation.surface: Someone helpless with laughter and delight is certainly not a sourpuss.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole closing exclamation: the person who spoils everyone's fun is never one overcome with laughter and delight.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoilsport who dampens fun is the very opposite of someone helpless with mirth.

clue.text: Arouse it and it'll eat wildly

indicators.note: wildly says the letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A tease: something about a dish arouses and it will be eaten ravenously.
explanation.definitionFit: To excite or stimulate someone pleasurably is to arouse them.

clue.text: King James, for example

definitions.meaning: a name borne by several English monarchs
the American-born novelist James, author of The Turn of the Screw

explanation.definitionFit: The name was borne by eight English kings, and the novelist James had it as his first name.

clue.text: Standard ecclesiastical sin — meanness

parts.note: par is a standard or norm, as in 'up to par'
simony is the sin of buying or selling church offices

explanation.surface: Listing a regular church sin alongside stinginess.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme reluctance to spend money is stinginess, a synonym for meanness.

clue.text: Having defective hearing, one abandoned the blower

indicators.note: something abandoned is left out, so the letter for one is dropped from the faulty trial

parts.note: a court hearing that is invalid because of an error is a mistrial
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone hard of hearing gives up on the telephone, the 'blower'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having defective hearing' looks like deafness but is a failed court case; 'the blower' looks like British slang for the telephone but is a wind. The MISTRAL is a cold wind of southern France.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong regional wind blows, so the wind is jokingly called the thing that blows.

clue.text: Fellow's suit

definitions.meaning: to go well with, as colours that complement each other

explanation.definitionFit: The word means an equal or counterpart, and as a verb to go well with something.

clue.text: Rigidity shown in second row with head

parts.note: a tiff is a minor quarrel, a row
a ness is a headland, a promontory, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: An argument in a back row makes someone's head go stiff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' rhymes with 'cow' here (a quarrel), not a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of flexibility, being hard to bend, is rigidity.

clue.text: Celebrate lifting of prize in America

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: in American spelling to prize something open is to lever it, and a prize is a lever

explanation.surface: A celebration as a prize is lifted aloft in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prize' looks like an award but is the American spelling of 'prise': to lever.
explanation.definitionFit: To make merry and party is to celebrate.

clue.text: Most generous and, to some extent, popular gesture

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A very generous act, and to a degree a crowd-pleasing one.
explanation.definitionFit: Large in the sense of liberal or bountiful, so the superlative is the most open-handed.

clue.text: In which three couples get together for sex

definitions.text: In which three couples get together for sex

parts.words: In which three couples get together for sex
parts.note: three couples make six, and in the old Roman tongue the word for six is spelt S-E-X, so this is the language where they combine to form that word

explanation.surface: A risqué description of group activity among three pairs.
explanation.definitionFit: In the classical Roman language the number six is written sex, so that tongue fits the riddle.

clue.text: Dog is sort of terrier? Vet'S entry is not conclusive

indicators.note: the shortened vet makes its entry into the rearranged terrier, going inside it
a sort of terrier is taken as a reworking of that word's letters
not conclusive means the word lacks its ending, so the last letter of vet is dropped

parts.note: taken as the word vet

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a dog is a kind of terrier, but the vet's record doesn't settle it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' looks like the subject of the question but is the definition. 'sort of' signals the anagram, 'is not conclusive' trims the vet's word, and 'entry' sends that trimmed piece inside the rearranged terrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A gundog breed bred to fetch shot game is a type of dog.

clue.text: Medusa's a sweet person!

parts.note: a jelly is a sweet dessert
fish is used of a person, as in 'a cold fish' or 'an odd fish'

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the Gorgon Medusa is really a lovely person.
explanation.walkthrough: Medusa is the mythical Gorgon, but medusa is also the zoological name for the free-swimming form of a jellyfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoologists call the bell-shaped, tentacled form of this sea creature a medusa.

clue.text: A self-treatment for invalid

indicators.note: a treatment works the letters over, so they come out in a new order

explanation.surface: Self-treatment as a remedy for someone who is ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invalid' looks like a sick person, linked to 'treatment', but it is the adjective meaning not valid.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim that is not true or not valid is wrong, untrue.

clue.text: Cause of ferment as yet unsettled

indicators.note: unsettled letters are disturbed and fall into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A ferment or unrest whose cause has not yet been resolved.
explanation.definitionFit: This fungus is the agent that makes dough and brewing liquids bubble and ferment.

clue.text: As divine female, I'm the one to call

parts.note: 'tis I' is an old way of saying 'it is I', I'm the one
to phone is to call

explanation.surface: Someone claims, as a goddess, to be the one to make the call.
explanation.walkthrough: TISIPHONE was one of the three Furies of Greek myth, avengers of murder.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the Furies, or Erinyes, she was a goddess of vengeance.

clue.text: Immediately at the scene of the action

definitions.text: at the scene of the action
definitions.meaning: physically present where something is happening

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both instantly, without delay, and present right where events are happening.

clue.text: Island's legislative assembly in America

definitions.meaning: the parliaments of the Channel Islands of Jersey and Guernsey are each called ...

explanation.definitionFit: Jersey and Guernsey each have a parliament called the States, and the phrase is also a familiar name for the USA.

clue.text: Financially far-sighted, having expert see books

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
vide is Latin for see, used in references
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone shrewd with money has an expert look over the accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is the Latin VIDE used in cross-references; 'books' is the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Being careful to save for the future is being thrifty and prudent with money.

clue.text: Tyre feels damaged, all-in

indicators.note: damaged suggests the letters are knocked out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: A damaged tyre feels completely worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all-in' looks like 'exhausted' but is a style of wrestling: all-in wrestling allows almost any hold, as does freestyle.
explanation.definitionFit: All-in wrestling is a style with few restrictions on holds, also called catch-as-catch-can or open style.

clue.text: Detectives, following young creature up, relaxed

indicators.note: following means the detectives come after the reversed young animal
in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, so reversed

parts.note: a calf is a young cow
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: Detectives tail a young animal, then unwind.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft and limp, lacking firmness, as a muscle that has gone slack.

clue.text: Thus about to become indifferent to pain

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for thus surrounds the word to

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as printed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Thus one is about to grow numb to suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the ancient Zeno school endured hardship without complaint, so the word means impassive in the face of suffering.

clue.text: It runs fast and sharp, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says a word sounding like the swindler is wanted, not the word itself

parts.note: a sharp, or sharper, is a swindler or card cheat

explanation.surface: Something runs fast and is keen, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sharp' looks like an adjective but is a noun, a card sharp; in non-rhotic British speech the swindler's word sounds like the big cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted big cat is the fastest land animal, so it is the one that runs fast.

clue.text: He told stories about river and ocean

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the river and the ocean together are read backwards

parts.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy
sea stands for ocean

explanation.surface: A storyteller who spun tales about a river and the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek fabulist is famous for short moral tales about animals.

clue.text: Finishing as you began, you stop when it's dawn

definitions.text: Finishing as you began, you stop when it's dawn

parts.words: Finishing as you began, you stop when it's dawn
parts.note: a night worker who started their shift as the sun went down finishes as the sun comes back over the horizon, the moment that is dawn

explanation.surface: A night worker's shift ends at first light.
explanation.definitionFit: The moment the sun rises above the horizon is the time of dawn.

clue.text: One beret I recollected as object of particular loathing

indicators.note: recollected read as re-collected means the letters are gathered again in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone remembers one beret that they particularly hated.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase, literally black beast, is used in English for a pet hate.

clue.text: British people provide support

parts.note: a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: The British nation lends its backing.
explanation.definitionFit: To prop or reinforce something is to strengthen it with struts, giving it support.

clue.text: Rocket launchers signal, finally, with sound of hooter

parts.note: NASA, the US space agency, launches rockets

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of the word signal

explanation.surface: Rocket launchers give a signal at last, with a hooter sounding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooter' is British slang for the nose, not a siren.
explanation.definitionFit: A voice that resonates through the nose, the slang 'hooter', has a twangy nasal tone.

clue.text: Showing agreement? Not I. for one

definitions.meaning: in accord or harmony with something
a letter that is not I, nor any other vowel: one such letter

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means in harmony or agreement, and the noun is any letter that is not a vowel such as I.

clue.text: Within a month, wife cleaned up

indicators.note: within puts the letter for wife inside the shortened month

parts.note: Sept is the short form of September

explanation.surface: Within a month the wife had tidied everything up.
explanation.definitionFit: Brushing with a broom is how a floor is tidied, so the past tense matches cleaned up.

clue.text: Remove outside page — it's empty

indicators.note: outside means the word for remove goes round the letter for page

parts.note: to delete is to remove or strike out

explanation.surface: Remove the outer page, since it's blank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' looks like an adjective describing the page but is a verb: to drain or use up.
explanation.definitionFit: To use up or exhaust a supply is to drain it, so the verb means to empty.

clue.text: Irregular mark for American's theme in school

indicators.note: in places the word for theme inside the short form of school

parts.note: a plot is the theme or storyline of a work, a sense especially current in American usage

explanation.surface: A grade given for an American's essay theme at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theme' in American schools also means an essay, which makes 'mark' look like a grade.
explanation.definitionFit: A blot or blotch of irregular shape is an untidy spot or stain.
